main_text.head: IN MENDACES.

p.i: Ignota Caelo, & ipsi Falsitas Solo, Illisque cunctis ille qua rerum parens Adstricta seruat Veritatis vinculo: Sed grata solis (prob scelus) mortalibus, Omnis magistra fraudis & Versutia, Quamplurimorum in corde & ore confidens. Impune in ipsos Principum irruens thronos, Clamosa Iudicum occupans subsellia, In officinis, in tabernis personans, Sacris & ipsis impudens ex pulpitis Surfum, deorsum, sancta Vertens omnia: Nunquamne mundo nisi ruente concides? Nam dia cuncta ceu tuetur Veritas, Sic cuncta dira Falsitate corruunt.

main_text.p: Regna ergo, regna quamdiu Deus sinet, Mundi hoc merente falsitate Falsitas, At, pauculi vos, Veritas quibus placet, Perstate fortes, Numinis freti manu. Nam tempus aderit, Mundus atque Falsitas Quum pariter vno corruent sic impetu, Vt illa Mundum, & Mundus illam pertrahat
main_text.head: IN GARRVLOS.
main_text.p: Quum fari decuit, tacere Velle: Velle, quum decuit tacere, fari:

page.notes: Large initial letters Q and I are decorative; the initial "I" of the first poem is a woodcut initial. The final word at lower right is partly cut off by the page edge and is uncertain. Some italic letters (e.g. long s rendered as s) are as printed.
